meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

examples.text: お前ら、一発逆転ホームラン頼んだぞ！
examples.trans: I'm counting on you guys for a comeback home run!

examples.text: これね、一発逆転ホームランになるかも。
examples.trans: This might really turn into that comeback home run.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Short for かもしれない; expresses possibility or uncertainty.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.en: be saved; be rescued; be a big help
meanings.note: Godan intransitive verb; 助かったよ means 'you saved me / that was a huge help'.

examples.text: 俺はトシだ。助かったよ。
手伝ってもらえて助かりました。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.note: First-person pronoun commonly used by men and boys in friendly or polite everyday settings.

examples.text: 僕もコーヒーをください。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Reflexive pronoun pointing back to the person under discussion.

examples.text: 自分の言葉で話します。
examples.trans: I speak in my own words.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Everyday noun for one's job or workplace duties.

examples.text: 新しい仕事は楽しいです。
これから仕事に行きます。
examples.trans: I am heading to work now.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Standard heartfelt apology.

examples.text: ごめんなさい、もうしません。
examples.trans: I'm sorry, I won't do it again.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: I-adjective; adverbial form うまく means 'well' or 'smoothly' (as in うまくいく).

examples.text: 計画がうまくいきました。
彼は英語がとてもうまいです。
examples.trans: He is very good at English.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

examples.text: ああ、うまくいった。君にもぜひ見てもらいたい自信作だ。
examples.trans: Yeah, it went great. It's a work I'm proud of and really want you to see.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.

examples.text: ああ、うまくいった。君にもぜひ見てもらいたい自信作だ。
examples.trans: Yeah, it went great. It's a work I'm proud of and really want you to see.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。
ボス、彼女が帰るそうで。
examples.trans: Boss, she says she's heading home now.

meanings.en: go home; leave and go back
meanings.note: Repeated past form 帰った、帰った! is an idiomatic shooing command ('off you go, go on home!').

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
そうか。またすぐかけ直す。
examples.trans: I see. I'll call you right back.
